headline: Highest risk is medium: Dify can write and egress broadly while Pathway is read-only/local, creating moderate prompt-injection and data-flow exposure but no direct write conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and ingest uploaded knowledge-base files, so malicious content could be treated as instructions if Pathway outputs are bridged into that workspace. Pathway itself has no file or network surfaces, so the interaction is one-way and indirect, but the shared datastore/workspace path makes injection plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are copied into Dify knowledge-base files or shared datastore entries
IF Dify workflows parse those files as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Pathway outputs into Dify prompts
Add provenance labels to all shared files
Restrict Dify to read-only references for Pathway-produced content
Review any parser that converts file text into tool instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, and it has broad network egress; Pathway is local-only with no egress or file access. If the pair shares a workspace or datastore, Dify can expose Pathway-derived sensitive content to external model providers, so leakage is plausible in default deployments even though Pathway itself does not transmit data.
conditions: IF Pathway-derived documents are stored in Dify knowledge bases or conversation logs
IF Dify sends those contents to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before handing data to Dify
Turn off external model providers for sensitive workflows
Separate Pathway storage from Dify workspaces
Audit Dify logs for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has filesystem write and shell execution, while Pathway has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no direct overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator maps both onto the same directory or datastore, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents
IF Pathway is extended with write access outside the documented profile
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only
Do not mount shared writable directories
Serialize any handoff through immutable files
Check for accidental concurrent writes in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act on tool outputs and external model responses, so if Pathway-produced text is treated as authoritative input, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated content. Pathway is a document-processing agent with no verification guarantees in the profile, so the pair lacks an explicit trust boundary even though the harmful path is indirect.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are fed into Dify prompts or workflows without validation
IF Dify uses those outputs to trigger tools, emails, or database writes
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Pathway and Dify
Require human review for any action-taking workflow
Mark Pathway outputs as untrusted by default
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation before Dify tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while Pathway is unverified and documents no data classes or residency controls. The main compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch if regulated data is routed into Dify; Pathway is not cited for a specific residency breach because its profile lacks such controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge bases
IF Pathway is used on data subject to residency or retention rules not documented for Dify
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Dify logs
Classify data before ingestion
Document retention settings for Dify
Review vendor terms for Pathway deployments
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the pipeline
